question: Scene B: baseline (StableNormal on mirror) beat nmask. Is that because the mirror is parallel to the +x wall it reflects (StableNormal <15 deg on 65% of mirror px)? Also: does larger camera height variation fix ceiling depth?
data: blender proj_indoor_mirror_b_rot30/dataset_r300 (mirror rotated 30 deg about vertical axis, furniture moved in front of mirror, camera height x3.5: 0.71-2.27 m above floor); EnvGS data/datasets/mirror_b/r300{,_nmask,_gtnorm}
prior_check: StableNormal vs GT mirror normal on mirror px: median 45.4 deg, <15 deg 2% (scene B: 9.0 deg, 65%), >60 deg 30% (B 32%)
eval: eval_mirror_b_run.sh with B=proj_indoor_mirror_b_rot30, val 38 frames (26 with mirror); per_obj/flatness/normal_spread with GT_PERSP=.../dataset_r300/persp
conclusion: Baseline no longer beats nmask: both turn the mirror into a virtual room (6.5% / 8.1% of mirror px on the plane, depth ~1.7 m behind), vs ~91% on plane in scene B. So B's baseline advantage was the parallel-wall coincidence. But nmask also collapses here (it did not in B), so B was easy even without a mirror prior; with the mirror at 30 deg and more objects in front, pure RGB prefers the virtual-room explanation. Only gtnorm gets the mirror (99.9%), and it also improves opaque PSNR by ~7 dB (the virtual room no longer competes with real geometry). Ceiling depth improves vs B (median error 0.67-0.75 -> 0.29-0.41 m) but >10 cm still on ~92% of ceiling px; confounded with the scene change. Motivates a prior-free mirror constraint (LiDAR mirror surface returns).
